S3_retail_projections.brief:
Material: eight-page marketing deck for the Lakeside Multifamily Income Fund, a private real estate offering sponsored and distributed by Northbridge Advisors, prepared by the banker.
Lane: retail — the questionnaire declares natural persons / more than 25 retail investors and distribution is by email and website, so RN 20-21 and the full SOP checklist apply notwithstanding the "accredited investors" line on the cover.
Already covered: essentially nothing. There is no disclaimers page, no forward-looking language, no past-performance line, no illiquidity or logo/testimonial legends and no source line on any page; the only risk reference is a pointer to the PPM on page 8, and page 6 partially discloses that some distributions came from offering proceeds.
Points that matter: page 1 and page 4 project investor returns (18% IRR, 2.1x, cash yields, cumulative distributions, exit value) — prohibited outright in a retail private-placement communication with no RN 20-21 exception available; the 7% distribution rate is called a yield and annualized while partly funded from offering proceeds; page 2 calls the preferred return "Guaranteed" and adds "can't-miss" plus a closing-date push; page 7 asserts the sponsor has never lost investor capital and averages 21% IRR from three of fourteen deals; page 5 testimonials claim market-beating returns with no legend.
Required additions: B9 illiquidity, B1 forecast, B3 past performance, B4 preferred return, B5 distributions, B7 testimonial legend, and A7 source lines on pages 4 and 7. The Tier A Finalis block is separately flagged as missing by the deterministic check.
Escalate: the volume and character of the issues — prohibited retail return projections plus a guarantee and a no-loss claim — go beyond wording fixes; recommend the reviewer treat this as a rebuild of pages 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 rather than a mark-up, and confirm whether the website channel is intended before any revised version is re-submitted.

inaccurate_picture.why: The deck shows only upside — projected 18% IRR, a "guaranteed" preferred return, an unbroken distribution history and a no-loss track record — with no risks, assumptions or illiquidity disclosure anywhere.

unsupported_claims.why: The no-loss claim, the 21% IRR from three of fourteen deals, the $600 million acquired, the property metrics and the testimonial's market-beating returns are all stated as fact with no source or basis.

promised_results.why: "Guaranteed 8% preferred return", "7% annual yield paid monthly" and "can't-miss opportunity" present returns to investors as assured outcomes.

Escalation: the post promotes a live private offering on an uncontrolled public channel with upside only and no risk language. The balance defect is clear under 2210(d)(1)(D) and RN 20-21, but whether the desk permits a public deal solicitation at all (general solicitation / offering-status question) is a supervisory call, not a machine call.

S6_email.brief:
Material: a short capital-raise email from the banker for Harbor Growth Fund III, first close in June, with a fund presentation attached (the attachment text is not in scope of this pass and its disclaimers are unverified).
Lane: institutional, deal-related, prepared by the banker; light review, no formatting or complexity points.
Already covered: the Finalis broker-dealer line is present on page 1.
Deterministic gaps already known to the desk: A1e email offering disclaimer missing, A3 institutional legend missing on page 1.
The point that matters most is the promissory framing: "Fund III will deliver 2.5x net" is an outcome stated as certainty and must be relabelled as a target.
Nothing in the email carries forward-looking, past-performance or risk wording, and there is no disclaimers page, so B1 and B3 have no coverage and must be added to the email body.
The three figures on page 1 carry no source line; A7 asks for the standard source text, not a disclaimer.
Escalate: the overall balance of an upside-only email (C9) and, once the return is relabelled a target, whether the criteria, assumptions and fee basis need to sit in the email or can rest on the attached deck (C19).
Recommend confirming that the attached presentation carries the disclaimers page and the institutional legend before release.

inaccurate_picture.why: A one-paragraph email states a future multiple, a prior-fund multiple and a close size with no assumptions, basis or risk, giving a more certain picture than the facts support.

unsupported_claims.why: The 2.5x, the 2.3x TVPI and the EUR 250 million are stated as fact with no source, as-of date or net/gross basis.

promised_results.why: "Fund III will deliver 2.5x net" promises a specific investor return.

S7_article.brief: Single-page article by Jane Doe (Northbridge Advisors) on private credit versus public bonds, ending with an implied 10% allocation suggestion. The A1r article/newsletter/educational disclaimer is deterministically missing and is the first required addition. Six findings; no institutional carve-outs apply. Nothing needs escalation on interpretation, but the headline itself has to change, so please confirm you are comfortable with the reframed title before it goes back to the banker.

quartus.brief:
Material: Quartus AI Fund II LP venture growth equity pitch deck, 28 pages, deal-related, prepared by the issuer/GP (Quartus Capital Partners LLC) and distributed by the banker. Lane: institutional (declared institutional-only, controlled distribution by email and meetings), so the lighter review applies: no formatting, emphasis or complexity points, fair-and-balanced judged once at document level.
Already covered: page 3 disclaimers (forward-looking statements, past performance not indicative, risk of loss, no assurance of targeted returns) and page 4 key risk factors including illiquidity; pages 9 and 25 footnotes cross-reference page 3 and state the basis of the projections; page 15 carries a Goldman Sachs source line; page 6 footnotes the Cambridge Associates benchmark. B1, B2, B3 and the illiquidity language are therefore not raised.
Required blocks (deterministic): the Finalis disclaimer with the broker-dealer line and the "For institutional investors only" legend on page 1 are both absent. Since the deck was prepared by the issuer, the Finalis disclaimer may instead go in the transmittal email, which must then also state that some or all of the attached material was prepared by a third party.
Points that matter: item-specific disclosures missing (B4 preferred return on page 27, B6 logo disclosure on page 23, B8 award substantiation on page 1); A7 source line missing on the page 16 chart; language points on pages 1/6/11/18/21/22 (pioneers, state-of-the-art, investor of choice, proven, delivers strong returns) and the unsourced "trillions of dollars" figure on page 6 and the peer-valuation comparison on page 22.
To confirm/escalate: page 27 sets a $100K minimum for individual investors while the questionnaire declares institutional-only, confirm the audience and the distribution controls before release. If the reviewer wants a second look at anything, it is the prominence of the 6.53x/7.65x Projected TVPI headline on page 9 next to the realized figures, which the desk currently treats as covered by footnotes 2 and 3 and page 3.

unsupported_claims.why: The "trillions of dollars" market figure on page 6, the "AI pioneers" cover line, the award on page 1 and the "lower valuation than our VC/PE peers" comparison are stated as fact with no source or basis on the page.

promised_results.why: "delivers superior risk-adjusted returns" (p11) and "designed to deliver strong risk-adjusted returns and return stability" (p18) state outcomes rather than objectives, though targets elsewhere are labelled and carry no-assurance language.

raised: "We believe … best" or "largest global institutions", page 6
"designed to deliver" with the illustrative legend, page 18
